title: Knowledge Tagging with Large Language Model Based Multi-Agent System

model.params_source: paper 'Implement Settings' (GPT-4o with temperature 0.7 for the numerical judger); temperature for the planner, solver and semantic judger not stated (0.0 assumed); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: all (concept, question) pairs of MathKnowCT: 24 knowledge concepts x ~100 questions (Table 1 counts, some concepts < 100)
task.approximation: Two demonstrations per concept are a seeded random draw (the paper's are unlisted); the paper adjusts prompt wording per LLM without printing variants; the numerical judger's generated Python is executed locally.

items.source: MathKnowCT (Li et al. 2024a) - no public release located on GitHub or Hugging Face on 2026-09-07

placeholders.question: question text (+ solver answer where 'Copied from Question Solver')
placeholders.example_1: labelled (knowledge, question, plan/judgment) demonstration 1, seeded random per concept
placeholders.example: one worked numerical-judging example in the Figure 3 style
placeholders.sub_constraints: numerical sub-constraints produced by the Task Planner
placeholders.argument: arguments extracted in Numerical Judger step 1
placeholders._note: five templates separated by '=== ... ===' headers; the final label is the AND of the semantic and numerical judgements

prompt.few_shot: k=2 examples per knowledge concept, randomly sampled from MathKnowCT (Dataset Overview)
prompt.source_location: Method section: Task Planner, Question Solver, Semantic Judger and Numerical Judger instruction templates
prompt.verbatim: partial (templates verbatim; the [Example] slots and the per-LLM wording adjustments are not printed)

output.parse: Semantic Judger: regex <(Yes|No)> (last match); Numerical Judger: stdout of the executed script (True/False); final = Yes only if all sub-judgements are Yes/True
output.postprocess: strip; execution error counted as False

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: (TP + TN) / (TP + FP + TN + FN) over all (concept, question) pairs.
metric.original_location: Table 4, block Multi-Agent LLMs, column GPT, row Accuracy / Large

open_points: MathKnowCT (Li et al. 2024a) could not be found as a public release (GitHub / Hugging Face, checked 2026-09-07); a human must locate it or drop the paper.
Protocol beyond one main stage: five dependent calls per item (planner, solver, semantic judger, two numerical-judger steps) plus local execution of generated Python.
